newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** India's Congress party will consider at a crucial meeting on Monday a call by senior leaders to review support to Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition government to discuss their five-month old ties but is unlikely to pull out of the coalition

Deve Gowda formed a minority United Front government in June with Congress' support after inconclusive April/May general elections returned his group with just 115 seats in the 545-member lower house of parliament

** The Indian Petroleum Ministry has officially scaled down this year's oil economy budget estimate from 35.65 million tonnes to 30.85 million tonnes, leading to a massive increase of about 28 billion rupees in the oil import bill, the Economic Times says

** The Finance Ministry has opposed a proposal by the Securities & Exchange Board of India to allow buyback of shares by promoters, saying that the Indian markets are immature and the regulatory framework too inadequate to monitor its orderly implementation, the Business Standard reports
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.69/70 per dollar on Monday. Dollar demand seen continuing with Monday's range expected at 35.67/71
** Indian shares are seen range-bound ahead of the Hindu new year this week, with investors not enthused by falling interest rates and better first-half company results
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index .BSESN fell 102.09 points or 3.14 percent last week to end at 3,148.57

** Merrill Lynch will soon pick up 40 percent equity stake in DSP Securities Ltd. This is likely to be followed by the addition of its own name to the stock brokerage firm to complete the organisational integration with the DSP group, the Financial Express reports
** Auto-component maker Sundaram Fastners Ltd to hold board meeting to declare first half 1996/97 (April-March) results later today
